How do you decide which of two strings comes first? You cannot compare whole strings with a single relational operator — you have to walk them byte by byte until they differ. What does that first differing byte tell you about the order? Remember an uppercase letter and a lowercase letter have very different byte values.

Where does this array stop? It has no length stored anywhere, so something marks the end. What is the very last slot, and how does your loop know not to read past it? What should happen when there is nothing, or only one thing, to sort?
